h1:
Phrae 2 Days 1 Night
Old City, Teak Houses & Chae Haeng
intro: Phrae is a compact, walkable town where the highlights cluster inside the old city or sit just a short drive away — which makes it perfect for a weekend escape. This plan puts Day 1 on the old city and ancient teak mansions, ending with the walking street, then Day 2 at Phra That Chae Haeng before picking up indigo-dyed cotton on the way home. Timing is realistic, the pace is unhurried, and rough food-and-entrance costs are built right in.

blocks.html: One of Phrae's best qualities is how close everything is. Khuem Chao Luang, Baan Wongburi, and the old-city temples are all within walking distance of each other. Wat Phra That Chae Haeng and Baan Tung Hong — the indigo-weaving village — sit on the edge of town, 15–20 min by car. Two days is genuinely enough to cover everything without rushing. A private car or rented motorbike makes the most sense here; Phrae has almost no local public transport to rely on.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Old City, Teak Houses & Walking Street

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: A relaxed walk through Phrae's old city

items.note: A teak mansion built in 1892 during the reign of Chao Phiriyadep Wongsa, combining Thai and European gingerbread architecture. The carved fretwork under the eaves and the decorative vents are remarkable. It now serves as the Phrae City Museum — allow about 45 min to wander and take photos.

A pink-painted colonial-Lanna mansion over a century old, dating to the Rama V era. The interior still holds original furniture and household objects. It's a short walk from Khuem Chao Luang; entrance is a nominal fee.

items.activity: Temples inside the old city walls — Wat Pong Sunan / Wat Phra Non
items.note: Several temples sit within or right beside the old moat, easy to visit back-to-back. The atmosphere is calm and unhurried — not overrun with tour groups.

Phrae's version of nam ngiao uses a clearer, lighter broth than Chiang Mai's. You'll find it around the back lane behind Narirattana School and near Pratu Chai gate. Order it with crispy pork rinds and a plate of fresh herbs — a full meal runs 40–60 THB.

An entire house built from solid teak, supported by 130 full-length teak trunks. Construction began in 1972, and it's now one of Phrae's most photographed spots. Open 08:00–17:00; entrance 20 THB for Thais, 40 THB for foreigners. About 10 min by car from the old city.
A Burmese–Shan-style prayer hall with stacked tiered roofs and intricate carved woodwork throughout. The architecture looks noticeably different from standard Lanna temples — worth the short detour.

items.activity: Coffee break in the old city
items.note: Phrae has a quiet café scene scattered through the old quarter. Streets around Kham Lue Road have several wood-house cafés — a good spot to rest your feet before the evening.

Runs Saturday evenings, roughly 16:00–20:00, along Kham Lue Road near Baan Wongburi. Expect local street food, handicrafts, and some live folk performances. If your trip doesn't land on a Saturday, find a northern restaurant in the old city instead.

blocks.title: Day 1 tip
blocks.html: Kad Kong Gao only runs on Saturday evenings. If catching the walking street is important to you, plan your first night to fall on a Saturday — you'll get the full atmosphere and best food selection.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Phrae trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Phrae
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Day 2 — Phra That Chae Haeng & Mo Hom Shopping

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Pay respects at the city's sacred chedi, then shop for souvenirs before heading home

items.note: Grab khao ngiao, rice porridge, or an old-school drip coffee in town before heading out. A light meal is enough before climbing the temple steps.

Phrae's most revered chedi and the birth-year temple for people born in the Year of the Tiger. The gilded stupa is striking up close. Open daily 06:00–19:00; no entrance fee. About 9 km from town — roughly 15–20 min by car. Allow time to climb the naga staircase and walk the terrace.

items.activity: Optional: Wat Phra That Doi Leng
items.note: Continue past Chae Haeng up the hill to Doi Leng for a wide-angle view over the Phrae valley — great for photos from above. Skip it if the mountain road feels too steep for your vehicle; this one is entirely optional.

Return to the old city and order northern Thai staples — hang lay pork curry, nam phrik noom with steamed vegetables, or kua yam spiced salad. A proper sit-down meal before the afternoon souvenir run.

items.activity: Baan Tung Hong — mo hom indigo cotton shopping
items.note: About 4 km from the old city, this village is the heartland of Phrae's mo hom fabric tradition — naturally indigo-dyed cotton using the hom plant. Shops line the main road selling shirts, bags, and accessories at reasonable prices. Mo hom is Phrae's most distinctive souvenir.

Beyond mo hom, popular Phrae gifts include khao kaep (crispy rice crackers), Chinese-style moon cakes, and other local snacks. Pick these up at Baan Tung Hong or souvenir shops in town before you leave.
Leaving Phrae in mid-afternoon gives you a comfortable drive or bus journey back without rushing.

blocks.title: Driving up to Chae Haeng & Doi Leng
blocks.html: The road to Wat Phra That Chae Haeng is smooth and easy. The climb to Doi Leng beyond it is steeper and winding. If you're not used to mountain driving, go early when visibility is good and check your brakes before setting off.

Phrae has accommodation ranging from guesthouses and hotels inside the old city to wood-house resorts on the outskirts. Staying in the old quarter works best for this itinerary — you can walk to the evening street market and stroll back without needing a car.

items.name: Hotels in the old city
items.blurb: Walking distance to Khuem Chao Luang, Baan Wongburi, and the walking street. Good choice if you don't have a car and want to explore on foot in the evening.

items.name: Wood-house resorts on the outskirts
items.blurb: Quiet, green surroundings and more privacy. Works well if you have your own transport; the drive into the old city is short.

items: Accommodation (1 night) — old-city hotels from around 500–1,200 THB/room (split between two people it gets cheaper)
Food (2 days) — around 400–700 THB eating mostly at local spots
Entrance fees — Baan Pratup Jai, Khuem Chao Luang, Baan Wongburi combined come to a few hundred THB at most
Transport / motorbike rental — rental bikes run around 200–300 THB/day, or fuel costs if you drove yourself
Souvenirs — budget 300–500 THB for mo hom fabric and local snacks, more if you fall in love with the textiles

blocks.html: All up, a budget Phrae weekend for one person lands around 1,500–2,500 THB. Two people sharing a room and splitting transport costs will bring that figure down noticeably.

items: Bus / minivan — daily services from Bangkok and Chiang Mai arrive at Phrae bus terminal
Flights — Phrae Airport has limited flights from Bangkok; check schedules in advance as they don't run daily
Private car — the most flexible option; parking is easy and sights are spread between the old city and the outskirts
Rented motorbike — available in town, ideal for moving between the old city and Chae Haeng without waiting for transport

faq.q: Is 2 days 1 night enough for Phrae?
faq.a: Yes, comfortably. Phrae's main draws are concentrated in the old city and just outside it. Two days covers the old-city temples, the teak mansions, Wat Phra That Chae Haeng, and a stop for mo hom shopping. If you want to add nature spots like Phae Mueang Phi or a waterfall, extend to 3 days 2 nights.

faq.q: Which night should I visit Phrae to catch the walking street?
faq.a: Kad Kong Gao runs on Saturday evenings along Kham Lue Road. Plan your first night to land on a Saturday and you'll get the best selection of food stalls and the liveliest atmosphere.

faq.q: What are the opening hours for Baan Pratup Jai and Wat Phra That Chae Haeng?
faq.a: Baan Pratup Jai (the Hundred-Column House) is open 08:00–17:00; entrance is 20 THB for Thais and 40 THB for foreigners. Wat Phra That Chae Haeng is open daily 06:00–19:00 with no entrance fee.

faq.q: Can I visit Phrae without a car?
faq.a: The old-city area is very walkable, so yes — you can cover most of Day 1 on foot. For Chae Haeng and Baan Tung Hong (both outside the centre), renting a motorbike is the easiest solution, or arrange a local songthaew or taxi for those legs of the trip.

faq.q: What should I buy as a souvenir from Phrae?
faq.a: Mo hom indigo-dyed cotton from Baan Tung Hong village is Phrae's signature product — shirts, bags, and accessories are all available at fair prices. After that, khao kaep crispy rice crackers and local Chinese-style pastries make good food gifts.
